column1: # ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.53 (c) — the pinned ABSENCE-SITE manifest for
# Columns: class <TAB> scope <TAB> fn <TAB> count <TAB> normalized-source
# The key is (scope, fn, source) — never a line number, which drifts on any edit above the site.
# CLASSIFICATION RULE (stated so the number is checkable, not asserted). A name absent from
# `grammar_tree` is absent for one of TWO reasons no site here can tell apart: the profile filter
# removed it, or it was never defined in this grammar (an `include(...)` external, which
# `node_satisfiable` treats as ⊤). The class turns on the DIRECTION the absence branch answers in:
#   verdict — it answers in the direction that RESTRICTS behaviour (dead / gated: prune a route,
#             exclude an edge, block a target). Being wrong here COSTS COVERAGE, silently.
#   guard   — it answers in the direction that declines to restrict: `continue`, an early
#             `return`/`?` yielding no answer, a `.filter(..)`/`.retain(..)`, an error, or a `false`
#             its consumer reads as "take the general path". Being wrong here costs nothing.
#   fixture — inside `#[cfg(test)]`: test plumbing, not engine logic.
# ⛔ THE POPULATION IS NOT THE DEFECT COUNT. 62 sites, 2 verdicts. Publishing 62 would mistake a
# population for a defect count; publishing only the 2 would leave the other 60 silently
# unexamined. Both are census-claim errors, in opposite directions — hence a full manifest.
# ⛔ A NEW `verdict` ROW IS THE EVENT THIS FILE EXISTS FOR. Classify it before pinning it, and read
# `mandatory_node_gated`'s own doc comment first: it records why the surviving conflation is latent
# and what would make it live.
